strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: Clearly articulates the limitation of global condition injection in multi-person scenarios and proposes local, identity-specific conditioning as the solution.

Elegant iterative mask prediction strategy: Cleverly resolves the chicken-and-egg dependency by using masks from step k to guide condition injection at step k+1, leveraging diffusion's multi-step nature without requiring ground truth at inference.

Strong empirical results on target task: Multi-person audio-driven generation shows substantial improvements (Sync-D: 6.67 vs 7.07/9.48 for baselines; FVD: 22.88 vs 40.24), with user studies showing clear preference (59.9% top-1 for audio-driven).
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Five evaluation dimensions, multiple test sets, rigorous ablations (Table 4) demonstrating component value, and both quantitative metrics plus user studies.
Large-scale dataset contribution: 2.6M video-entity pairs with per-frame masks addresses a real data gap for human-centric video research.
Solid technical quality: Appropriate choice of focal loss for imbalanced supervision, well-designed training procedure with frame alignment flags, and sound overall approach.
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-written paper with good figures, extensive supplementary materials, detailed implementation information, and thoughtful experimental design.
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: Individual components are standard (self-attention for reference injection, cross-attention+MLP for mask predictor, prior-work audio conditioning). Main contribution is problem recognition and component combination—solid engineering but incremental.

Incomplete evaluation of mask prediction: No direct evaluation of mask quality (e.g., IoU vs ground truth during training), making the core mechanism largely unexamined. Mask accuracy is critical but only evaluated indirectly through downstream metrics.

Small multi-concept test set and user studies: Only 100 samples for multi-concept evaluation and 10 users with 19/9 video samples respectively—below standards for strong claims about multi-concept capabilities.

Training data limitations: Predominantly 2-3 people per video, limited text prompt diversity, ranked 2nd in prompt following (Table 3). These constraints limit generalization and trade off text fidelity for audio-visual alignment.

Arbitrary hyperparameter choices: Mask injection threshold (step 10), CFG strength (6.5), loss weights (1:1), appearance ratio (0.7:0.3) lack ablations or justification. No analysis of mask convergence across diffusion steps.

Limited scope of multi-concept claims: Despite the title, most results focus on multi-person audio scenarios. Limited demonstrations of human-object interactions or non-human objects. Method appears optimized for audio-driven rather than general multi-concept generation.

Missing key experimental details: No computational overhead analysis despite 50 diffusion steps; no sensitivity analysis for critical hyperparameters; limited failure case analysis; no statistical significance testing on modest test sets; ID embedding baseline surprisingly weak but not deeply investigated.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple test sets, diverse metrics (Sync-C/D, CLIP-I, DINO-I, FVD, IQA, AES), user studies, and thorough ablations with strong quantitative results (Sync-D: 6.670 vs 9.482 for OmniHuman)

Strong empirical results on multi-person scenarios: 30% improvement in lip-sync, better overall video quality (FVD: 22.881 vs 40.239), maintains competitiveness on single-person benchmarks, 59.9% user top-1 preference

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty of individual components: Mask predictor is straightforward cross-attention+MLP; reference injection is standard self-attention; audio conditioning directly from OmniHuman via wav2vec. Baseline comparison limitations: ConceptMaster and Video-Alchemist unavailable limiting direct comparison; multi-concept comparisons somewhat unfair since those methods lack audio support; user study with only 10 evaluators; subject consistency evaluation on only 9 videos is small sample

Limited analysis of failure modes and edge cases: No systematic evaluation on occlusions, extreme poses, rapid movements, or non-frontal faces; scaling beyond 3 people shows only marginal gains, suggesting method may not generalize well to larger groups
